description:
Two beliefs resting on exactly the same evidence, with no contradiction between them.

Rules out a criterion that fires on evidence sharing alone. Two beliefs can rest on the same observations and agree completely - that is corroboration, not underdetermination, and it is the commonest shape in any real web. If the criterion derives a meta-belief here, it is reading overlap and calling it conflict.

One of the two negatives that pin both halves of the criterion as load-bearing; `conflict_disjoint_evidence` is the other. Neither is decoration: a criterion passing every positive fixture while failing one of these is measuring something other than what it claims.

expect.note: Structural. The evidence condition is satisfied and the conflict condition is not.

evidence.summary: The distant supernovae are dimmer than a static model predicts.
The dimming is the same in every direction we have measured.

beliefs.proposition: The observed dimming is a real effect rather than an instrumental artifact.
The dimming measurement is reproducible across the observed fields.
